title: Repeated abrupt termination in EKS, v28.0 due to bad DNS

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> Unable to resolve host: <redacted-host>

Seems like a DNS resolving issue? Running Typesense on Kubernetes requires some care. I recommend using this community maintained operator: https://github.com/sai3010/Typesense-Kubernetes-Operator

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hi @participant1, thank you for taking a look! 💜 

You mean

```
Unable to resolve host: <redacted-host>
```

right? I took these logs from typesense-2 (crashed) while typesense-0 was still restarting after the update to v28, so K8s had temporarily removed the DNS record from the headless service. We had these messages with v27 as well during re-deploys, and they would resolve over time when the pod would be available again. Hence, personally I think this is unrelated, but you're the expert of course :)

As said, we also we experienced these crashes while testing v28-rc37 before, also during "normal" operation. While the cluster was running without load, the pods would individually randomly crash about once every other hour perhaps.

FWIW, here's out manifests: https://gist.github.com/reporter/efbee049c9cb47e7b08fee25a20f64de

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: These crashes are k8s specific and we don't have too much operational issue on Kubernetes. Running a raft service on k8s is tricky because the underlying Raft library we use requires IPs of pods to be persistent across restarts, which is at fundamental odds with the kubernetes operations. That's why I suggested using a stable community maintained operator which takes care of these requirements.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Side-node: I definitely took inspriration from sai3010/Typesense-Kubernetes-Operator while building this cluster, but it's not really working for us; e.g. the readiness probe [here](https://github.com/sai3010/Typesense-Kubernetes-Operator/blob/main/templates/statefulset.yaml#L57-L62) is too quick for the pod to become ready and K8s would keep restarting the pods.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: There's one more recent project you can look at: https://github.com/akyriako/typesense-operator

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Sure, will do and see if they do anything different from us. 👍  Thank you. Already see that they're dynamically updating the nodes list, maybe that's something I could try.

Let me just repeat that this is definitely a regression from v27, it was working fine there.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: We have not actually changed anything in this code in some time, definitely not for the v28 release.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @participant1, can Typesense ignore the failed DNS resolution (which should be temporary) instead of returning an empty peers list and crashing?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: That crash happens inside the Raft library we use, where the DNS resolution happens. We don't have a control over that.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: ah, is that separate to the DNS resolution that happens here: https://github.com/typesense/typesense/blob/de5815c0d47f33de4055fce197c5b2ab493c02b1/src/raft_server.cpp#L182-L183

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: In this particular case, we are just pushing the string as it is, and not returning an empty peers list. That logic is inside the library.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
so is the logic here:

1. if's an ip, just add the ip
2. if it's a hostname, resolve and add the ip
3. if we can't resolve, just add the hostname

in what case would 3 be useful vs just not adding the peer? in the k8s case, if we just send the two alive peer IPs instead of two alive peer IPs and one unresolvable peer hostnames, wouldn't that fix the issue?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Yeah we can try doing that. Do you have an environment where this problem occurs often that you can test to verify that it works once we have a build with this patched?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: yes, this is quite easy to repro in my environments. It seems to mostly be a problem if it takes typesense a few extra minutes to come back (which is typical of managed K8s environments where persistent disks need to be detached from one host and reattached to another).

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Ok I will make this change and share a build in a few days.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Please check against `29.0.rc9`?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I can verify as well. I run 3 typesense (virtual) servers on 3 separate machines and have had random weird crashes in 27 and 28. Twice on 28.

I'll upgrade to 29.0.rc9 and see if it fixes it.

Group default_group fail to issue RPC to 10.X.Y.Z:8008:8108 _consecutive_error_times=1, [E2][10.X.Y.:8008][E2]peer_id not exist [R1][E2][10.X.Y.Z:8008][E2]peer_id not exist [R2][E2][10.X.Y.Z:8008][E2]peer_id not exist [R3][E2][10.X.Y.Z:8008][E2]peer_id not exist

In our case, it's just an IP, no dns resolution.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @participant1, 29.0.rc9 worked well, I can see the "unable to resolve host" line when one of the pods go down, but it doesn't kill the other two. Is there a timeline when 29.0 will be released?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Thanks for confirming @participant2 -- we don't have a release date for v29. We usually just accumulate enough changes before doing a release.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Is it possible to hotfix onto v28 then? While this has been happening for some time in production so maybe the urgency isn't high, I still want to roll it out but I'm not sure the RC is safe enough.
